All three verified against source.

## 1. `deleteComment` — no, it does not verify who wrote the comment

`ArticleService.deleteComment()` at `src/article/article.service.ts:114-129` takes exactly two arguments — `slug` and `id`. There is no caller identity in the function at all:

- `src/article/article.service.ts:117` — loads the comment by id
- `src/article/article.service.ts:118` — the only comparison in the method is `_comment.id === comment.id`, i.e. locating the comment inside `article.comments`, not an ownership check
- `src/article/article.service.ts:121-122` — splices and deletes unconditionally

The controller doesn't supply identity either: `deleteComment(@Param() params)` at `src/article/article.controller.ts:85` has no `@User()` parameter, unlike its neighbours `favorite`/`unfavorite` (`article.controller.ts:94`, `:102`).

Two reinforcing facts:
- **It couldn't check even if it wanted to.** `Comment` (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15`) has `id`, `body`, and a `@ManyToOne` to `ArticleEntity` — there is no `author` relation and nothing writes one (`addComment` at `article.service.ts:104-105` sets only `body`). So there is no stored owner to compare against.
- **The `403 Forbidden` annotation is decorative.** `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` at `src/article/article.controller.ts:83` documents behaviour no line implements.

What *is* enforced is authentication only: `DELETE articles/:slug/comments/:id` is in the `AuthMiddleware` list at `src/article/article.module.ts:29`. Net effect — any logged-in user can delete any comment on any article.

## 2. Profile routes with the auth middleware

`ProfileModule.configure()` registers exactly one matcher (`src/profile/profile.module.ts:20-22`):

```ts
.forRoutes({path: 'profiles/:username/follow', method: RequestMethod.ALL});
```

Mapped against the controller (`src/profile/profile.controller.ts`):

| Route | Handler | Guarded |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `follow` — `profile.controller.ts:23-26` | **Yes** (covered by `RequestMethod.ALL`) |
| `DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `unFollow` — `profile.controller.ts:28-31` | **Yes** (same matcher) |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `getProfile` — `profile.controller.ts:18-21` | **No** |

`getProfile` is public but still reads `@User('id')` (`profile.controller.ts:19`) — on an unguarded route the decorator decodes the token itself, so `userId` is `undefined` when no token is sent. The `@ApiBearerAuth()` on the class (`profile.controller.ts:11`) applies to all three in Swagger and does not reflect the actual middleware coverage.

## 3. The `RO` suffix

`RO` = **Response Object**. It marks the interface as the RealWorld response envelope — the top-level wrapper key the spec requires — rather than a bare entity. Concretely, in `src/article/article.interface.ts`:

- `ArticleRO` → `{ article: ArticleEntity }` (`:24-26`)
- `ArticlesRO` → `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` (`:28-31`)
- `CommentsRO` → `{ comments: Comment[] }` (`:20-22`)

and `ProfileRO` → `{ profile: ProfileData }` in `src/profile/profile.interface.ts:8-10`. Request bodies mirror the same nesting via `@Body('article')` / `@Body('comment')` (e.g. `article.controller.ts:77`). A handler returning a bare entity breaks every RealWorld frontend, which reads `response.article.slug`.

One caveat worth flagging: `ArticleRO.article` is typed as `ArticleEntity`, not the `ArticleData` interface declared just above it at `article.interface.ts:7-18`. So `ArticleData`'s spec-correct field names (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `favoritesCount`, `favorited`) are never actually applied to a response — the entity's own names go out on the wire instead. That's the spec-conformance item already listed in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.

**Not read:** `profile.service.ts`, `user.interface.ts`, `auth.middleware.ts` (middleware behaviour above is from `.claude/knowledge/auth.md`, not re-verified in source this turn), and the `prisma/` folder.
